title: Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major
hook: A quiet march that grows into a festival, and one of the most famous slow movements Mozart wrote.

painting.title: The Swing
painting.pairingNote: A young woman flies up on a swing in a sunlit garden; the lightness and play of the concerto’s outer movements, and the dream of its Andante.

facts: Mozart finished it in Vienna on 9 March 1785, about four weeks after the dark D minor concerto, K. 466. He played it the next day, 10 March, at a concert of his own in Vienna’s Burgtheater. Like the D minor concerto, it was written for his own concerts that season.
It is a festive concerto in C major, with trumpets and drums in the orchestra, but much of it is quiet. The first movement opens with a march played softly, on tiptoe.
Mozart’s own cadenzas for it are lost, so every pianist has to supply them. Géza Anda plays his own in this recording.

The slow movement became famous far beyond concert halls when the Swedish film *Elvira Madigan* (1967) used it, in this very recording by Anda. The concerto is still sometimes called the “Elvira Madigan” concerto.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a quiet march that becomes a celebration (I), a long, dreaming song over muted strings (II), a bouncing comic-opera finale (III).

movements.heading: Allegro maestoso
movements.summary: A grand first movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a [[double-exposition|double exposition]] that begins very quietly: a march on tiptoe in the strings. The full orchestra, with trumpets and drums, soon takes over, and the piano enters with a little flourish of its own. Along the way there is a sudden turn to the minor.

mainIdeas.name: The march
mainIdeas.description: a short, tiptoeing figure in the strings, all playing the same notes.

mainIdeas.name: The fanfare
mainIdeas.description: an answer in the wind instruments, then the whole orchestra with trumpets and drums.

mainIdeas.name: The minor-key surprise
mainIdeas.description: a sudden dark tune in G minor in the middle of the piano’s exposition.

mainIdeas.name: The piano’s tune
mainIdeas.description: a graceful, singing melody in G major.

stops.hear: Strings alone, very quiet: a short marching figure, all playing the same notes
The winds answer with a little fanfare; then the whole orchestra, with trumpets and drums, takes up the march
The orchestra quietens; the march seems to tiptoe away
stops.happening: The end of the orchestra’s exposition

stops.hear: The piano enters with a short flourish of its own, ending on a trill, while the orchestra plays the march underneath
stops.happening: The piano’s entry. Its first notes are a brief lead-in, a miniature [[cadenza|cadenza]]

stops.hear: Suddenly darker: a tense, minor-key tune
stops.happening: A turn to G minor that looks forward to Mozart’s Symphony No. 40

stops.hear: A graceful, singing tune in the piano
stops.happening: The second theme, in G major

stops.hear: Running notes in the piano move through minor keys while the orchestra adds fragments of the march
The quiet march returns in the home key
The orchestra stops on a held chord; the piano plays alone, freely, and ends on a long trill

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The orchestra alone; the march dies away quietly

notice: Listen to the very end. After all the trumpets and drums, the movement closes as quietly as it began.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Anda plays the piano and directs the orchestra from the keyboard, as Mozart did; there is no separate conductor.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A long, dreaming melody over a soft, pulsing accompaniment. The violins play [[muted|muted]], the middle strings pulse in groups of three, and the cellos and basses pluck. The piano takes up the song and wanders through distant keys before coming home.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: long and slow, with wide leaps, first in the muted first violins.

mainIdeas.name: The pulse
mainIdeas.description: repeated notes in groups of three in the second violins and violas, with [[pizzicato|pizzicato]] in the cellos and basses.

mainIdeas.name: The wandering
mainIdeas.description: in the middle, the piano drifts into minor keys, with sharp clashes in the harmony.

stops.hear: A slow, veiled melody in the violins over a soft pulse in threes and plucked basses
The piano takes up the melody, high and clear, over the same pulse
The melody drifts into minor keys; wide leaps and clashing notes
stops.happening: The middle section, moving through C minor and G minor

stops.hear: The melody returns, now in a warmer, unexpected key
The music finds its way home and fades

notice: Listen under the melody. The pulse in threes hardly ever stops, like a heartbeat under the song.
In the middle the harmony rubs: notes that clash with each other and resolve late. They are part of the movement’s ache.

notes.title: One word, many names
notes.body: Mozart called the movement simply “Andante”. The name “Elvira Madigan” comes from the 1967 film, not from him.

movements.heading: Allegro vivace assai
movements.summary: A quick, bouncing [[rondo|rondo]] full of comic-opera energy. The orchestra opens with a jumping tune; the piano answers, and soloist and orchestra keep tossing ideas back and forth until a brilliant ending.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a jumping, cheerful tune in the full orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The piano’s answers
mainIdeas.description: quick scales and runs, and a new, playful tune of its own.

mainIdeas.name: The minor episode
mainIdeas.description: a brief, stormier passage between the returns.

stops.hear: The full orchestra plays a quick, jumping tune
The piano plays a short flourish alone, then enters with a tune of its own
stops.happening: The piano’s entry, through a short [[cadenza|cadenza]]

stops.hear: A new, playful idea in the piano, answered by the winds
stops.happening: The first episode, in a new key

stops.hear: The jumping tune returns
A brief, stormier passage in the minor
The refrain once more, passed between piano and orchestra
stops.happening: The last return of the refrain

stops.hear: The orchestra stops; the piano plays alone, then the tune returns

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A rush of rising scales and loud final chords

notice: Listen to the conversation. The piano and the woodwinds keep interrupting each other, like characters in a comic opera.

threads.title: Quiet beginnings
threads.body: The first movement starts on tiptoe, the slow movement with muted strings. Mozart saves the brilliance for later.

threads.title: Trumpets and drums
threads.body: They give the outer movements their festive ring, and they are silent in the Andante.

threads.title: Who has the tune?
threads.body: In the first movement the orchestra presents the march and the piano decorates it; in the Andante the piano takes over the song; in the finale the two share and trade it.
